task: Prepare me for a meeting with Attio (attio.com)

merged.claim: Attio is an AI-native, agentic CRM for go-to-market teams. It compounds customer signals into context and acts on them across the pipeline, building pipeline, advancing deals and growing accounts around the clock.

Nicolas Sharp is CEO & Co-founder of Attio. He authored the Series B announcement and the Oct 2026 agentic-revenue launch, and says Attio is building a CRM with first-class agentic access across every surface.

Alexander Christie is Co-founder & CTO of Attio. He authored the Oct 2026 architecture post (Project Centaur, SQL, Data Connectors, Interfaces) and discussed Universal Context and the future of CRM on the Founders & Builders podcast.
Drew Peterson is Attio's VP of Sales & Success, based in San Francisco (in role since Jul 2024).
Przemek Owczarek is Attio's Director of Engineering, based in Krakow (director since Mar 2025).
Alex Vale is VP Marketing at Attio (per his personal site, dated Sep 22, 2026).
Shriya Anand is Attio's Chief of Staff. She announced the fourth Graduate Associate cohort and describes early-career hiring as core to Attio's talent philosophy.
Eoghan Mulcahy, Inconvo co-founder, joined Attio Engineering in July 2026 and is excited to help shape how AI becomes part of the CRM experience.
Liam Mulcahy, Inconvo co-founder, joined Attio Engineering in July 2026, citing Attio's technical depth and care for users.
Michael McBride of GV joined Attio's board with the Series B. He is noted for scaling GitLab's revenue more than 100x through its IPO and beyond.

Priority: build the hybrid architecture for agentic revenue, with software for people and agents together. It is a high-scale, directly queryable data platform for agents and analytics: SQL Engine / Project Centaur (Postgres-compatible SQL), live Data Connectors, Agent Scale, Activities (beta), and API/MCP access.

Priority: make AI-agent Workflows a core product pillar and the operating layer for orchestrating revenue agents (prospecting, lead triage, briefings, follow-up, stalled-deal revival, signal-based outreach). 'The new Workflows' shipped Jun 9, 2026.
Priority: expand and smooth Ask Attio, the AI assistant. It has more model choices (Claude Opus 4.7 option), custom context, suggested follow-ups, a ChatGPT store listing and an MCP surface.

Priority: invest in engineering and AI primitives, expand globally and hire product talent. The Series B funds scaling engineering, global expansion and AI-primitives development. Attio has a London HQ (~196-206 employees), distributed engineering, and is hiring a Product Lead.

Priority: build the talent pipeline. In Aug 2026 Attio opened its fourth Graduate Associate cohort, hiring across GTM Engineering, Customer Success & Support, Partnerships, Growth, Campaigns, Lifecycle and operations.

Priority/change: Formula Attributes (July 2026, announced with the Jul 28 release alongside new workflow blocks, mobile performance work and more Ask Attio models). They give deterministic calculations, reporting, workflow triggers and sequence personalization for forecasting and agentic work.

Priority: expand the integration ecosystem and cross-tool automation through new workflow apps (Resend, ClickUp, Google Sheets, Asana, Hunter), Aircall AI call summaries in notes, and a stable App SDK 1.0.0.

Priority: win the 'AI-native CRM vs legacy CRM' category battle (calling CRM a $58B category at a do-or-die moment) and court GTM builders via GTM Atlas content. It serves 5,000 paying customers including Lovable, Granola, Modal, Replicate and Public.

Recent change (Sep 23, 2026): Attio shipped workflow history and agent log, with visibility into every workflow run down to the agent step (tools called, records changed, credits used), plus new workflow blocks including call recording and meeting linking.
Recent change (Sep 23, 2026): Attio added Resend and ClickUp workflow apps, Aircall now writes AI call summaries into notes, and Ask Attio suggests what to ask next.
Recent change (Aug 25, 2026): Attio shipped new Workflows apps (Google Sheets, Asana, Hunter), expanded workflow controls, new API/MCP capabilities and stable App SDK 1.0.0.
Recent change (Aug 25, 2026): native dictation was added to Ask Attio, removing the need for an external transcription tool.

Challenge: failed email delivery and mailbox disconnections were not visible enough. The Aug 25, 2026 release added a Failed tab for emails that failed after all retries and clearer disconnect feedback; frequency and severity are not established.

Recent change (Oct 2026, ~Oct 15): Attio repositioned its homepage around 'agentic revenue' and launched its architecture page and posts. They feature Project Centaur, Postgres-compatible SQL, live Data Connectors, Interfaces (Activities and Interactions), and agents operating with user-level permissions across Ask, MCP, API and Workflows.
Recent change (Jul 2026): Attio repriced plans: Free (3 seats), Plus $44 monthly/$35 annual, Pro $99 monthly/$79 annual, Enterprise custom, with extra workspace credits from $70/mo.

Challenge: the July 2026 price increase caused buyer confusion, with third-party listings and Attio's comparison page contradicting each other on seat limits. Reviewers also flag AI/workflow credit consumption as a budget surprise.

Challenge: proving price-to-value for simpler CRM use cases. An April 2026 reviewer found Attio hard to justify at ~€1,000 per seat annually for a focused workflow and built the needed functionality with Claude Code.
Recent change (Jul 9, 2026): the Inconvo team (co-founders Eoghan and Liam Mulcahy) joined Attio Engineering in an acqui-hire to strengthen agent and AI access and the integrations ecosystem.
Recent change (Jul 10, 2026): Attio acquired Ten.dev per PitchBook. It also completed a secondary transaction on Mar 1, 2026 and reports 196 employees.
Attio raised a $52M Series B led by GV (announced Aug 2025; $116M raised to date), citing 5,000 paying customers and on track for 4x ARR growth.

Challenge: reviewers (G2, Capterra) cite enterprise/mid-market feature gaps: field permissions, validation rules, multi-currency conversion, formula fields, reporting, and mandatory pipeline fields by stage.

Challenge: outbound/sequencing and the integration ecosystem are thin. Limits are 12 emails/hour and 10 people per sequence, there are no native Sales Navigator, Apollo or Lemlist connections, and far fewer marketplace apps than HubSpot (1,500+).

Challenge: reliability and support concerns. A Dec 2025 G2 reviewer cited unreliable service with no SLA or downtime compensation. A Dec 8, 2025 Trustpilot review reported a bug-caused outage, lost leads and poor support.
Challenge: competitive pressure from Salesforce/HubSpot and legacy CRMs (manual inputs, rigid workflows), other AI CRM alternatives, and a fragmented GTM tool ecosystem requiring costly integrations.

Challenge: turning agentic capability into reliable, governed work at scale. This means meeting scale, reliability and concurrency demands (shared transactional view for concurrent agents), permissions, inspectable agent actions, and trade-offs among speed, safety and performance. Activities remain in beta; these are stated engineering requirements, not an outage.
Challenge: contact import and onboarding friction. A Jan 2026 customer review reported failed contact uploads, broken mapping and unhelpful errors.
Challenge: maintaining product simplicity and best-in-class customer experience as product surface and technical complexity (data models, schemas, APIs) expand.

Attio challenge: it must translate ambitious agentic-platform capabilities into dependable outcomes at scale. c1.note: The homepage says "The CRM for agentic revenue" and describes a platform that builds pipeline, advances deals and grows accounts around the clock. It doesn't use the words "AI-native", but the substance matches.

c2.note: Nicolas Sharp authored the Oct 2026 agentic-revenue post, which describes a hybrid architecture for people and agents. The phrase "first-class agentic access" isn't verbatim. The Series B post is Aug 2025, so it is not recent. I didn't open the Inconvo post.

c3.note: Alexander Christie, CTO & Co-founder, authored the Oct 2026 post covering Project Centaur, SQL, Data Connectors and Interfaces. I didn't check the podcast link.

c4.note: The source is an internal dataset I can't open. A web search found no Drew Peterson at Attio.

c5.note: A Krakow-based Przemek O. with an Attio connection exists, but no title or start date is visible, so "Director of Engineering since Mar 2025" is not confirmed.

c6.note: Page says he is currently VP Marketing at Attio. It gives no date, so the Sep 22, 2026 date could not be confirmed.

c7.note: Shriya Anand is Chief of Staff and announced the fourth Graduate Associate cohort in a post from August 2026, within 90 days. I did not check the talent-philosophy wording.

c8.note: The post is from July 2026 and says Eoghan Mulcahy joined Engineering. His quote about shaping how AI becomes part of the CRM matches. July is about 90 days before today, so it sits at the edge of the window.

c9.note: Liam Mulcahy's quote about technical depth and care for users matches the post. Same edge-of-window timing as c8.

c10.note: The McBride board detail is accurate. However, the Series B was published in August 2025, about 14 months ago, so it is not current and falls outside the 90-day window.

c11.note: The Oct 2026 post covers SQL Engine, Data Connectors, Agent Scale, Activities (beta) and MCP/SQL access. It doesn't mention the name 'Project Centaur', which is a minor detail in the claim.

c12.note: The changelog lists 'The new Workflows' on Jun 9, with follow-up updates through Sep 23. The Jun 2026 blog post confirms the agent use cases. The launch itself is outside 90 days, but the work is ongoing.

c13.note: The changelog confirms Opus 4.7 (Apr 16), the ChatGPT store (Apr 29), custom context (May 28), more models (Jul 28) and suggested follow-ups (Sep 23). It also confirms the MCP server (Feb 19).

c14.note: The Series B post is from Aug 2025, over a year old, so it is not current. The use of funds matches, but the page doesn't give the headcount. The Product Lead role is open, with no posting date.

c15.note: The Aug 2026 post opens the fourth Graduate Associate cohort. The roles match, and it also lists Office of the CEO, Product Operations and General Operations.

c16.note: Formula attributes launched Jul 28, 2026 (changelog) and the blog post is dated Jul '26, which is inside the 90-day window. The extra details about workflow blocks, mobile performance and more Ask Attio models were not confirmed.

c17.note: App SDK 1.0.0 (Aug 25, 2026) and the Resend, ClickUp and Aircall AI summaries (Sep 23, 2026) are confirmed. Google Sheets, Asana and Hunter were not found on the cited pages.

c18.note: The $58B and do-or-die wording is there, but the post dates from July 2024 (updated Aug 2026). It does not mention 5,000 customers, the named customers or GTM Atlas, so the claim is not shown to be current.

c19.note: Workflow history and agent log are confirmed for Sep 23, 2026, including tools called, records changed and credits used. The call recording and meeting linking blocks are not on this page.

c20.note: Resend, ClickUp and Aircall AI summaries are confirmed for Sep 23, 2026. The Ask Attio suggestions entry is also dated Sep 23 on the changelog.

c21.note: The Aug 25, 2026 changelog lists new Workflows apps and blocks, new API/MCP capabilities and App SDK 1.0.0. The pages didn't name Google Sheets, Asana or Hunter, so those names are unconfirmed.

c22.note: The Aug 25, 2026 entry says dictation is now native in Ask Attio, with no external transcription tool needed.

c23.note: The Aug 25 entry adds a Failed tab for emails that failed after all retries and clearer mailbox-disconnect feedback. It gives no evidence of how often this happens or how bad it is, so calling it a challenge is an inference.

c24.note: The blog post (Oct 2026) confirms Project Centaur, the Postgres-compatible SQL engine and Interfaces. The architecture page confirms 'agentic revenue', live Data Connectors and agents acting with the same permissions as people. The building-attio-s-architecture URL returns 404, and the ~Oct 15 date and the homepage repositioning are unconfirmed.

c25.note: A third-party article dated Oct 6, 2026 confirms a July 2026 repricing and the quoted USD prices, with credit packs from $70/mo annual. It is secondary sourcing; Attio's own pricing page showed EUR prices that match.

c26.note: A tldv article checked on Oct 5, 2026 confirms the July 2026 repricing (Plus $44, Pro $99), the 10-seat cap on Plus, and credit burn from AI and workflow use. Coffee.ai separately reports Attio's table saying 'up to 10 seats' while its FAQ says 'unlimited seats'. Coffee.ai does not call the change a price increase, and the two sites quote different prices.

c27.note: The review is real: Nicolò Mazzari, Apr 20, 2026, 2 stars, about $1,000 per user per year, built with Claude Code. But it is a single review dated about 184 days ago, outside the 90-day window, so it is not current evidence of a challenge.

c28.note: The Inconvo acqui-hire is real, and the post says the Mulcahy co-founders joined Engineering. It is dated July 2026 (the claim says Jul 9), about 104 days ago, which is outside the 90-day recent-changes window.

c29.note: The Attio PitchBook page returned 403 and the fetch tool returned empty content. A search found a Ten.dev profile showing an acquisition completed Jul 10, 2026, but it does not name Attio as the buyer. The date is also more than 90 days old. The secondary transaction and 196 employees were not checked.

c30.note: The facts are accurate: $52M Series B led by GV, 5,000 customers, 4x ARR, $116M raised in total. But the round was announced in Aug 2025, over a year ago, so it is not a recent change. It is only background context.

c31.note: The article quotes a G2 review from July 2026 and a Capterra review from Nov 2025 on these gaps. The source sells a competing CRM, and some of the reviews are older than 90 days.

c32.note: The article cites the 12 emails/hour limit (G2, May 2026) and the 10-person sequence limit (Capterra, Mar 2026). It also states there is no Sales Navigator connector and that HubSpot has 1,500+ apps. These come from a competitor's article, and the review dates are older than 90 days.

c33.note: The Trustpilot review exists and describes a bug-caused outage, lost leads and poor support. It is dated Dec 10, 2025, with Dec 8 as the likely incident date. That is outside the 90-day window. I could not find the Dec 2025 G2 reviewer claim in the article.

c34.note: The article confirms competition from HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive and folk. The Series B post (Aug 2025) mentions legacy CRMs with manual inputs and rigid workflows, but not fragmented GTM tools or costly integrations. The pressure is ongoing, and the Series B source is not recent.

c35.note: Attio's Oct 2026 posts cover scale, concurrency, a transactional view, same permissions for agents, inspectable queries, and Activities in beta. They don't discuss trade-offs. The challenge is inferred from Attio's design goals and is not a reported problem.

c36.note: The review is real (Jan 26, 2026, 'Can't upload contacts'). But it is about 9 months old, outside the 90-day window, and it is a single review, so it is not a current visible challenge.

c37.note: The posting only lists aspirational job duties (thoughtful simplicity, best-in-class experience). It does not show Attio struggling with this, and it has no date. This is an inferred pain, not an evidenced challenge.

c9.note: Attio's blog (dated Jul '26) says Liam and Eoghan Mulcahy are joining Attio Engineering. It quotes Liam on the team's 'technical depth' and 'genuine care for users.' The post gives no day. The 90-day cutoff is Jul 23, so this is borderline, but press coverage suggests the deal was reported around August 2026.

c18.note: The post (from Jul 2024, updated Aug 2026) does say CRM is a $58B market at a 'do-or-die moment.' But it never mentions GTM Atlas, and it gives no count of 5,000 customers and doesn't name Lovable, Granola and the others. Those figures come from the Aug 2025 Series B post, so the claim merges two sources.

c30.note: The details are accurate: GV led, $116M raised to date, 5,000 customers, on track for 4x ARR growth. But it was announced in August 2025, more than a year ago, so it fails the 90-day rule.

c32.note: The coffee.ai article (updated Oct 2026) supports this: no native Sales Navigator, Apollo or Lemlist integrations, and HubSpot has 1,500+ marketplace apps. The 12 emails/hour and 10 people per sequence figures come from G2 and Capterra user reviews, not official limits.
